title: Brain–Computer Interfaces for Traumatic Brain Injury and Spinal Cord Injury: Lesion-Pattern Matching, Functional Restoration, and Clinical Translation
title_zh: 脑机接口用于创伤性脑损伤和脊髓损伤：病灶模式匹配、功能恢复与临床转化
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being developed for clinically relevant assessment, communication, rehabilitation, and functional restoration after central nervous system injury. However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. This narrative review examines BCI applications in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) using an injury-pattern-guided framework that links residual neural architecture with clinical tasks, interface selection, and outcome assessment. MAIN BODY: In SCI, motor intention and cortical activity may remain accessible despite disruption of descending pathways, supporting motor-intention decoding, brain-controlled functional electrical stimulation, neuroprosthetic control, and brain-spine interfaces. In TBI, diffuse and heterogeneous network dysfunction shifts the clinical emphasis toward detection of covert consciousness, assisted communication, neurofeedback, and multimodal rehabilitation. We compare non-invasive, endovascular, electrocorticographic, and intracortical recording approaches; summarize evoked-response, motor-imagery, and continuous decoding paradigms; and distinguish functional substitution from closed-loop restoration of an individual's own movements. Recent invasive systems have supported the restoration of grasping, standing, and walking in selected individuals with SCI, whereas evidence in TBI remains concentrated on brain-state assessment and low-bandwidth communication. CONCLUSION: Clinical translation will require careful candidate selection, stable long-term recordings, effective bidirectional feedback, clinically meaningful real-world outcomes, ethical oversight, and sustained technical support. Disease-specific translational pathways, rather than a universal BCI model, are likely to provide the most practical route to routine clinical use after central nervous system injury.
abstract_zh: 背景：脑机接口（BCI）正越来越多地被开发用于中枢神经系统损伤后具有临床相关性的评估、沟通、康复和功能恢复。然而，其临床角色在不同损伤类型间差异显著。本叙述性综述采用损伤模式指导框架，探讨了创伤性脑损伤（TBI）和脊髓损伤（SCI）中的 BCI 应用，该框架将残留神经架构与临床任务、界面选择和结果评估相关联。主要正文：在 SCI 中，尽管下行通路受损，运动意图和皮层活动仍可能可及，支持运动意图解码、脑控功能电刺激、神经假肢控制以及脊柱脑接口。在 TBI 中，弥漫且异质的网络功能障碍将临床重点转移到隐匿意识检测、辅助沟通、神经反馈和多模态康复。我们比较了非侵入性、血管内、硬膜下皮层图谱和皮质内记录方法；总结了诱发反应、运动想象和连续解码范式；并区分了功能替代与个体自身运动的闭环恢复。最近的侵入性系统支持了部分 SCI 患者握持、站立和行走的恢复，而 TBI 的证据仍集中于脑状态评估和低带宽沟通。结论：临床转化将需要仔细的受试者筛选、稳定的长期记录、有效的双向反馈、具有临床意义的现实世界结果、伦理监督和持续的技术支持。疾病特异性转化路径，而非通用 BCI 模型，很可能是中枢神经系统损伤后常规临床应用最实际的途径。
